# Pinned Coney regression input

`coney.json.gz` contains the original OSM response and nine separate NYC source responses used by the map regression tests. `manifest.json` records queries, acquisition timestamps, counts and a SHA-256 checksum of the uncompressed JSON. Each response retains its own source metadata and original properties. Node's built-in gzip support reads it; no download is needed to run offline tests.

This fixture is test input, not an automatic data source for the map page. Live queries and explicit `map-capture.mjs` exports remain separate. Refreshing this fixture is a deliberate baseline change: review geometry/provenance differences and expected assertions, then regenerate its checksum. Do not replace it implicitly when public datasets change.

`building-identity.json` is a small, separate September 2026 capture near Hampton Avenue and Hastings Street. It retains four OSM buildings and five corresponding NYC footprints, including a shifted identity match, a split footprint, weak overlap and a placeholder BIN. Query provenance and source metadata remain in the file. It exercises matching behavior rather than serving as a benchmark scene.

OSM data © OpenStreetMap contributors, available under the [Open Database License 1.0](https://opendatacommons.org/licenses/odbl/1-0/). See [OpenStreetMap copyright and attribution](https://www.openstreetmap.org/copyright). NYC records are attributed to NYC Open Data and the NYC Department of City Planning's LION service; dataset identifiers and query URLs appear in the manifest. Consult the [NYC Open Data terms](https://opendata.cityofnewyork.us/overview/#termsofuse) and each dataset's metadata for its terms and limitations.

Vercel deployment and the optional npm release artifact exclude this directory. Browser-based regression tests inject it explicitly from the local Node runner.

`transport-inventory-input.json.gz` and `transport-inventory-manifest.json` retain exact scoped ramp, roadway and bridge records from NYSDOT, complete layer metadata, original native/GeoJSON batch requests, capture times, attribution and an uncompressed SHA-256 checksum. They exercise source completeness and role boundaries independently of the earlier Coney/fidelity captures. They are test input only. Full query responses remain in the ignored local transport investigation.

`native-layer-samples.json.gz` and `native-layer-manifest.json` retain complete scoped MTA station records/metadata and two original NOAA NYC 2017 LASzip payload samples, EPT schema/CRS, complete origin inventory and the captured intersecting source-tile metadata. URLs, timestamps, attribution and checksums are recorded. Deterministic tests construct a small additive hierarchy around the binary samples; this is not a complete recorded point-cloud hierarchy or a production fallback. Full live area captures remain ignored local artifacts, separate from earlier inputs.

`planimetric-samples.json.gz` and `planimetric-manifest.json` retain selected unmodified NYC native/geographic records, complete layer metadata and source requests, selected pedestrian survey/program records and metadata, plus the complete bounded MTA entrance capture. Native source coordinates and geographic Z remain distinct channels. Deterministic test inventories are constructed for those selected records; full live queries remain ignored evidence under `.tmp/map-lab/open-review/captures/`. The manifest records capture bounds/dates, source attribution and an uncompressed checksum. This is separate from earlier inputs and is never loaded automatically by the map page.

`land-context-samples.json.gz` and `land-context-manifest.json` add selected unmodified records from the original NYC land/context services, with full layer metadata, native/geographic geometry, source requests, attribution and checksums. Tests construct bounded inventories for those samples, including the cartographic pavement service's distinct `OBJECTID_1`. Complete area queries remain under ignored `.tmp/map-lab/close-findings/captures/`; the page never loads this fixture automatically. This addition does not overwrite earlier fixtures.

`fidelity-input.json.gz` and `fidelity-manifest.json` are a separate native-mesh/equipment/bridge capture. They preserve complete intersecting 2014 I3S node JSON and binary geometry/attributes, current Luna footprints, live 2022 water-tank layer/native/GeoJSON responses, and mapped Verrazzano bridge/support ways with NYC bridge observations. The manifest records request URLs, acquisition evidence, attribution and an uncompressed SHA-256 checksum. The bridge fixture intentionally selects bridge spot observations; full ground/roadbed captures remain in the local research bundle. This fixture does not overwrite the original Coney/crash baseline.
